titleStmt.title: CONTINGENCY STATEMENT OF THEMES APPROVED BY THE SECRETARY OF STATE AS OUR PUBLIC POSITION IN THE EVENT OF INTERVENTION IN LEBANON

div.head: CONTINGENCY STATEMENT OF THEMES APPROVED BY THE SECRETARY OF STATE AS OUR PUBLIC POSITION IN THE EVENT OF INTERVENTION IN LEBANON

list.label: A.
list.item: Lebanese Government has complained to/notified United Nations Security Council of large-scale militaristic interference from outside Lebanon which has disrupted peace and security of Lebanon and which gravely threatens independence of that country.
list.label: B.
list.item: Both the United States and United Kingdom have received requests for aid from the President and (legitimate) government of Lebanon within the context of the Lebanese Government’s complaint to the Security Council regarding the threat to its integrity and independence.
list.label: C.
list.item: The United States Government, in response to the Lebanese request and in the light of the situation in Lebanon, has agreed to send certain combat forces to Lebanon in order to protect American life and property and to assist the Lebanese Government in its military program for the preservation of the independence and integrity of Lebanon. The United Kingdom has also agreed to send military units to Lebanon for similar purposes.
list.label: D.
list.item: This action is consonant with the provisions of the United Nations Charter. It relates to the need to preserve the independence of Lebanon against aggression, and has no purpose connected with the Lebanese internal political situation.
list.label: E.
list.item: As soon as the purposes for which these military units have been dispatched to the Lebanon are accomplished, the units will be immediately withdrawn.
list.label: F.
list.item: It is noted that the Lebanese Government has received declarations of sympathy and support from other states in the area.

note.p: Top Secret; Limit Distribution; Eyes Only.
British reserve position on this point. [Footnote in the source text.]
